newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO UNHAPPY WITH OWN FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO UNHAPPY WITH OWN FANS.

text.p: Hamburg will be hoping Monaco's fickle fans turn against their own side as easily in next week's UEFA Cup clash as they did during their French first division match at the Louis II stadium on Wednesday night.

Brazilian striker Anderson and teenager Thierry Henry, who scored their first goal in the 52nd minute of a 2-0 home win over Strasbourg, both complained afterwards at the crowd's jeers and whistles when they did not take an early lead.
But the pair asked not to be quoted, fearing perhaps that would only make matters worse when Monaco meet Hamburg in the first leg of their UEFA Cup third round tie in the principality next Tuesday.

Monaco, who played in front of only 2,500 on Wednesday, have generally fared better away this season, clinching their berth in the third round with their 4-2 away win over another German side, Borussia Moenchengladbach. They lost the home leg 1-0 two weeks later.
Coach Jean Tigana said: "(The crowd) have been terribly spoilt lately. They have to understand also that the players are tired. I have few replacements with so many injured."

Monaco, who hit a purple patch last month with successive 4-1 wins in the league after the 4-2 victory in Germany, have central defender Emmanuel Petit and playmaker Enzo Scifo definitely out of next Tuesday's match.

France's other UEFA Cup contenders Metz won at home in the league for the first time in more than two months, 2-0 against Rennes, in front of Kevin Keegan, manager of their third-round rivals Newcastle United.

Metz's recent run of good form has included inflicting on champions Auxerre their first home defeat of the season last week. They are now fourth, although 10 points adrift of leaders Paris Saint-Germain.

"The most important thing was to taste victory again at home and pull away from the teams in mid-table," said coach Joel Muller, whose side's last home win was over Sporting Lisbon in their UEFA Cup second-round first-leg match on October 15.
